newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Telebras is undervalued - ING.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Telebras is undervalued - ING.

text.p: ING Barings said it has raised its 12-month price target for Brazil's Telebras to $175 per American Depositary Receipt (ADR), showing a 22.5 percent growth rate and potential total return of 40.5 percent.

Pat Jurczak, ING Barings' head of Latin American telecom research, said the current stock price includes "huge discounts" for all Telebras operations but a new valuation of its cellular services will give it an immediate boost.

"A cellular valuation of $33 to $45 per potential subscriber (POP), the result of Brazil's cellular B Band auctions, should produce an immediate six to 12 percent increase in stock price," he said in a report.

The Dutch investment bank said Telebras has only $13 per POP reflected in its current price, compared with the $22 per POP minimum price set by the government for concessions to operate on the B Band frequency.
"At these levels, Telebras' 'sum-of-the-parts' stock price would be between $134 to $139 per ADR, an immediate $10 boost on today's stock price," the report said.
ING Barings gave the following "break-up" valuation of Telebras operations at its current average price of about $125 -- long-distance $28, local $84, and cellular $13.
In June, the government is expected to announce the winners of the first B Band cellular licenses. Brazil has auctioned 10 concession areas and has received bids from 15 consortia on nine of them.
Telebras' ADR was up 1-3/4 at 128-3/4 in New York while its preferred rose 1.55 percent to 138.00 reais and its common was up 0.78 percent at 129.30 reais in Sao Paulo at 1506 local/1806 GMT.
